<reason>A won a competitive debate by making spreading look like ordinary capacity management, splitting the trip into a fixed icon and relocatable hours, and trapping B on seasons plus elasticity. B’s best hit—that the core stays packed so diffusion only drafts new streets—was real, but B never fully answered seasonal spreading or “where the next visitor goes,” and the clipped second rebuttal left A with the cleaner path: managed diffusion versus a sacrifice zone plus stay-home.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A’s first-rebuttal elasticity trap plus the 90-minute/40-hour split, which forced B to defend pricing the basilica while claiming complements cannot move and the core must stay a permanent scrum.</best_rebuttal>
